candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Uprava za statistiku Crne Gore (Statistical Office of Montenegro), institutional portal
candidates.why_relevant: Legally mandated producer of Montenegrin official statistics and the master hub for every demand-side denominator needed to normalise card/POS/ATM statistics: population, households, retail turnover, tourism, ICT usage, national accounts. Bilingual (cg/eng) mirrored URL structure (page.php?id=NNN) makes it systematically crawlable and the natural entry point for snowballing to every sub-domain.
candidates.legal_status: official statistics; reuse normally permitted with source attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled crawl of the eng/ and cg/ page.php?id= tree plus /uploads/files/ PDF and XLS release paths; parse release PDFs/XLSX rather than HTML tables.
queries_used: MONSTAT upotreba informaciono-komunikacionih tehnologija domaćinstva Crna Gora
Statistical Office of Montenegro MONSTAT

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Upotreba informaciono-komunikacionih tehnologija: domaćinstva i pojedinci (ICT usage in households and by individuals)
candidates.why_relevant: The single most directly payment-relevant MONSTAT survey: annual Eurostat-aligned ICT household survey covering internet access, device use, online purchasing (e-trgovina/kupovina preko interneta) and online-payment behaviour by individuals. Supplies the e-commerce adoption denominators behind card-not-present growth. 2024 release documents 84.5% household internet access on a ~1,200-household sample.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF/XLSX harvest of the ICT release directory by year folder; extract e-commerce and online-payment indicator tables.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query (local language) + snowball to metadata page
queries_used: MONSTAT upotreba informaciono-komunikacionih tehnologija domaćinstva Crna Gora

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Upotreba IKT u preduzećima (ICT usage in enterprises)
candidates.why_relevant: Merchant-side counterpart to the household ICT survey: e-business, e-commerce sales, website/online-ordering capability and barriers to ICT use among Montenegrin enterprises. This is the closest official proxy for merchant acceptance readiness (which merchants can take card-not-present orders) outside the central bank's acquiring data.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF harvest from /uploads/files/ICT/<year>ent/ ; extract e-commerce sales share by NACE size class.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search + snowball from ICT domain page
queries_used: Monstat "informaciono društvo" upotreba IKT preduzeća saopštenje 2025 e-trgovina kupovina preko interneta

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Promet u trgovini na malo (retail trade turnover releases)
candidates.why_relevant: Monthly/quarterly retail turnover in current and constant prices, and by commodity group (food, motor fuel, pharmaceuticals/cosmetics). This is the denominator for card-spend-to-retail-turnover penetration ratios and for judging whether card volume growth is real or price-driven. Recent releases report Q2 retail turnover +7.2% current / +4.1% constant y/y.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly scrape of the retail-trade release list plus /uploads/files/trgovina/ PDF+XLSX; keep the commodity-group breakdown series.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query (local language) + site menu fetch
queries_used: MONSTAT promet u trgovini na malo saopštenje

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Promet u trgovini na veliko (wholesale trade turnover)
candidates.why_relevant: Wholesale turnover complements retail as a B2B payments denominator (credit transfers, commercial cards) and helps separate consumer from business flows when interpreting aggregate payment-system value data.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly release harvest alongside retail trade.
queries_used: MONSTAT promet u trgovini na malo saopštenje

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Turizam: dolasci i noćenja turista (tourist arrivals and overnight stays)
candidates.why_relevant: Montenegro's payment card market is structurally seasonal and foreign-cardholder-heavy; ~95.8% of 2025 overnight stays were by foreign tourists (2,728,564 arrivals / 15,367,166 overnights). Monthly arrivals and overnights by nationality are the essential normaliser for non-resident card acquiring volumes, ATM cash withdrawals in coastal municipalities and seasonal POS deployment.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly harvest of /uploads/files/TURIZAM/ releases (PDF+XLSX) and the eng/novosti.php news items; retain country-of-origin breakdowns.
queries_used: Montenegro MONSTAT tourism arrivals overnight stays monthly release cruise 2026

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Anketa o potrošnji domaćinstava (Household Budget Survey)
candidates.why_relevant: Household income, expenditure and consumption structure by COICOP purpose — the demand-side base for consumer payment capacity, wallet share by category and cash-intensity of spending categories. Conducted since 1983; since 2015 on a multi-year cycle (roughly every 2-3 years) with 1100/380-household samples, so cadence is low but structural value is high.
candidates.legal_status: official statistics; microdata likely only via formal research request
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Event-driven harvest on each survey wave; also archive the methodology PDF to interpret category definitions.
queries_used: MONSTAT anketa o potrošnji domaćinstava household budget survey Montenegro publikacija

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Statistički godišnjak / Statistical Yearbook
candidates.why_relevant: Single consolidated annual PDF carrying long back-series across every domain (population, trade, tourism, national accounts, ICT, finance). Ideal for one-shot historical backfill of denominators instead of scraping dozens of individual release series, and bilingual sr/en in one file.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual download of the yearbook PDF (large, table-heavy — use table extraction, not naive text parsing).
queries_used: Monstat "Mjesečni statistički pregled" OR "Statistički godišnjak" 2025 publikacija PDF

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Mjesečni statistički pregled (Monthly Statistical Review / Bilten)
candidates.why_relevant: Monthly cross-domain bulletin published since 2008 and reported by MONSTAT's own user survey as its most-used data source. Gives one predictable monthly artefact bundling retail turnover, prices, tourism and labour indicators — a low-cost high-frequency monitoring anchor for the whole cell.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Deterministic monthly URL pattern fetch of /uploads/files/Bilten/YYYY/M/BILTEN BR N.pdf with fallback to the publications index.
queries_used: Monstat "Mjesečni statistički pregled" OR "Statistički godišnjak" 2025 publikacija PDF

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Kalendar objavljivanja / Statistical Release Calendar
candidates.why_relevant: Legally required advance publication calendar. Turns the whole MONSTAT estate from blind polling into scheduled collection: tells the collector exactly when retail turnover, tourism, ICT and national accounts releases land, and flags methodology changes and postponements.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Parse annually into a scheduling table that drives the crawl of the other MONSTAT series.
queries_used: MONSTAT statistical release calendar

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Metapodaci / metodološka dokumentacija (metadata & methodology explorer)
candidates.why_relevant: Per-survey metadata pages (legal basis, sample, periodicity, definitions, data sources). Critical for knowing whether an indicator is comparable across years and which administrative body actually supplies the underlying data — several metadata entries name external suppliers (e.g. customs revenue overview supplied by the customs administration), which is a snowball vector to fiscal sources.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate prikazi_metapodatke.php entries once, store as a survey registry, re-check annually for methodology breaks.
queries_used: Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore godišnji izvještaj o radu statistika broj fiskalizovanih računa

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Popis stanovništva 2023 / Census and demography (population and household counts)
candidates.why_relevant: The 2023 census and the demographic estimates series give the population and household base for every per-capita payment metric (cards per capita, ATMs per 100k inhabitants, POS per 1000 inhabitants) and — via municipality-level counts — for coastal-versus-inland acceptance density analysis.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off deep harvest of census result tables plus annual population-estimate release; store municipality-level population.
candidates.discovered_via_method: site menu fetch (Census data / Demography sections)
queries_used: Statistical Office of Montenegro statistics sections census demography

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Nacionalni računi / National accounts (GDP and components)
candidates.why_relevant: GDP, GNI and household final consumption expenditure are the standard denominators for payment-system value ratios (payments/GDP, card turnover as % of household consumption) and for cash-in-circulation-to-GDP comparisons used in cash-usage analysis.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly and annual release harvest; retain household final consumption expenditure separately from GDP.
queries_used: MONSTAT national accounts GDP Montenegro

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT — Cijene / Prices (CPI, HICP) and Registri (statistical business register)
candidates.why_relevant: Two supporting series in one cell area: CPI/HICP to deflate nominal card and retail values into real terms, and the statistical business register (broj privrednih subjekata by activity and municipality) which is the merchant-population denominator for POS penetration ('POS terminals per active retail enterprise').
candidates.source_subtype: price indices + statistical business register publications
candidates.legal_status: official statistics; register aggregates public, unit-level records not
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly CPI release fetch; annual business-register publication fetch with NACE x municipality breakdown.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct fetch of MONSTAT registers page + menu
queries_used: MONSTAT indeks potrošačkih cijena
MONSTAT registri privrednih subjekata

candidates.source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore (Ministry of Finance) — institutional site and document library
candidates.why_relevant: Publisher of monthly budget execution reports, quarterly/annual central and general government debt reports, the budget law and the Economic Reform Programme (PER) with its macroeconomic and fiscal framework chapters. Provides the fiscal backdrop and forward macro projections against which payments-market growth is judged; reported Q1 2026 gross public debt of EUR 5,133.5m (59.9% of GDP).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monthly crawl of the ministry's document library sorted by published_at; grab monthly budget-execution XLSX/PDF and quarterly debt reports.
queries_used: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore makroekonomski bilten javne finansije mjesečni
gov.me Ministarstvo finansija "bilten" javnih finansija izvještaj o javnom dugu publikacije

candidates.source_name: Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore (Revenue and Customs Administration) — fiscalization authority
candidates.why_relevant: Operator of Montenegro's mandatory electronic fiscalization system (in force since 1 June 2021), in which EVERY invoice — cash AND cashless — is reported to the tax authority in real time and receives a unique fiscal identifier. This is the only national dataset that structurally distinguishes cash from cashless transactions at invoice level across the whole retail economy; even aggregate disclosures from it would be the highest-value cash-usage evidence outside CBCG. Also publishes customs revenue collection overviews that MONSTAT itself reuses.
candidates.source_subtype: tax and customs administration / fiscalization operator
candidates.access_status: institutional site public; underlying invoice-level fiscalization data NOT public — aggregate disclosure would require an information-access (slobodan pristup informacijama) request
candidates.legal_status: microdata protected by tax secrecy; only official aggregates or FOI responses are collectable
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor news/annual work reports for aggregate fiscalization figures; consider a formal free-access-to-information request for cash vs cashless invoice counts and values. Do NOT attempt to access the EFI self-service portal.
candidates.discovered_via_method: first-principles inference (who must record every transaction) + local-language search
queries_used: Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore elektronska fiskalizacija efi statistika bezgotovinsko plaćanje
Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore godišnji izvještaj o radu statistika broj fiskalizovanih računa

candidates.source_name: elektronskafiskalizacija.me — official e-fiscalization information portal (SEP/EFI)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative documentation layer for the fiscalization scheme: technical specifications, payment-method (način plaćanja) code lists used on every fiscal invoice, business-premises (poslovni prostor) and cash-register/ENU registration rules. The payment-method taxonomy is directly relevant to how card, cash and account-transfer transactions are officially classified in Montenegro, and the registration rules define what counts as a POS-equipped premises.
candidates.access_status: informational pages public; SEP portal itself requires qualified certificate login
candidates.legal_status: public-sector information; portal login area out of scope
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off harvest of the technical specification and code lists, then diff on version changes. Public info pages only — never the authenticated SEP portal.
queries_used: Uprava prihoda i carina Crne Gore elektronska fiskalizacija efi statistika bezgotovinsko plaćanje
candidates.observed_blocker: SEP/EFI self-service area requires a qualified digital certificate (issued via Pošta Crne Gore); only the public Info/* pages are collectable.

candidates.source_name: Data.gov.me — Portal otvorenih podataka Crne Gore (national open data portal)
candidates.why_relevant: Legally established central open-data portal where public bodies — including the Ministry of Finance and statistical/fiscal administrations — publish machine-readable datasets. CKAN-based, so it exposes organisation and tag filters and, typically, a REST API, making it the cheapest structured-ingest route into Montenegrin public-sector data and a discovery index of which body publishes what.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate organisations and datasets via the CKAN API (package_list/package_show) rather than HTML; subscribe to new-dataset polling.
queries_used: data.gov.me otvoreni podaci Crna Gora Monstat skupovi podataka

candidates.source_name: Eurostat — enlargement countries statistics (Montenegro)
candidates.why_relevant: Independent aggregator that re-publishes MONSTAT's transmitted data (including the ICT household survey, national accounts and trade) in harmonised, EU-comparable form with a documented API/bulk-download layer. Solves two problems at once: cross-country benchmarking of Montenegro's card/e-commerce penetration against peers, and a cleaner machine-readable channel than scraping MONSTAT PDFs.
candidates.legal_status: Eurostat reuse policy — free reuse with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Pull Montenegro (geo=ME) series from the Eurostat dissemination API for ICT household/e-commerce, national accounts and trade tables; use Statistics Explained pages only for context.
queries_used: Eurostat enlargement countries Montenegro database statistics ICT households retail trade

candidates.source_name: MONSTAT news / saopštenja feed (novosti.php and novosti_arhiva.php)
candidates.why_relevant: Chronological index of every MONSTAT release with stable numeric ids, mirrored at /eng/novosti.php. The most reliable single change-detection surface for the entire office: cheaper and more complete than watching a dozen domain pages, and each item links straight to the underlying PDF/XLSX.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll the archive index daily, diff on the id sequence, and enqueue newly appearing release attachments; a monthly archive page exists at index.php?month=M&year=YYYY.
candidates.discovered_via_method: recurring appearance across searches + URL-pattern inference

candidates.source_name: Montenegrin economic press as secondary relay of MONSTAT/MoF releases (RTCG, CdM, Portal Analitika, MINA, Montenegrobusiness)
candidates.why_relevant: These outlets restate MONSTAT and Ministry of Finance figures within hours of publication, often quoting numbers whose source PDF is hard to locate on the institutional site, and occasionally reporting official statements that never appear as a formal release. Useful as a low-latency tripwire and as a cross-check that a number was actually published — never as the primary figure of record.

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Keyword monitoring on 'MONSTAT', 'promet u trgovini na malo', 'javni dug', 'fiskalizacija'; always resolve back to the institutional primary document before recording a figure.
candidates.discovered_via_method: search-result snowball across multiple local-language queries

negative_findings.description: Searched in Montenegrin for a Ministry of Finance monthly macroeconomic bulletin analogous to Serbia's 'Bilten javnih finansija'. No such standing monthly bulletin surfaced for Montenegro; search results were dominated by the Croatian and Serbian finance ministries. What the Montenegrin ministry does publish appears to be monthly budget-execution reports, quarterly/annual public-debt reports and the Economic Reform Programme.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Montenegrin MoF 'makroekonomski bilten' identified; the cell's fiscal cadence rests on budget-execution and debt reports instead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The seed query assumed a bulletin that may not exist under that name; collection design should target the ministry's document library by document type rather than waiting for a named bulletin.

negative_findings.description: No public statistical output was found from the electronic fiscalization system (in force since 2021) breaking transactions down by payment method — i.e. no official cash-versus-cashless invoice counts or values published by the Revenue and Customs Administration. All located material is vendor guidance and compliance how-tos (Telekom, Pošta Crne Gore, ERP vendors), not statistics.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fiscalization payment-method aggregates appear to exist as data but not as publications.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This is the single richest potential cash-usage dataset in Montenegro and it is currently dark to open collection; a free-access-to-information request is the realistic route and should be planned deliberately.

negative_findings.description: No evidence surfaced of a PxWeb-style interactive statistical database or public API at MONSTAT; dissemination appears to be page.php HTML index pages linking PDF and XLSX files under /uploads/files/ and the legacy /userfiles/file/ paths.
negative_findings.result_summary: MONSTAT looks document-oriented rather than database-oriented; no API confirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection cost is materially higher (PDF/XLSX parsing, two legacy path conventions) and Eurostat's Montenegro series become the preferred machine-readable channel where coverage overlaps.

negative_findings.description: MONSTAT page ids are not stable across the cg/ and eng/ trees or over time: the id=475 page resolved to construction activity (2012 archive) in English while local-language results associate 475 with retail trade, and file assets are split between the legacy /userfiles/file/ and current /uploads/files/ roots.
negative_findings.result_summary: Numeric page ids and asset paths are unreliable long-term identifiers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector keyed on page ids will silently drift onto the wrong domain; keying on the saopštenje/novosti archive index and on release titles is safer.

negative_findings.description: No Montenegrin-language official statistical term was found for POS-terminal or ATM counts within MONSTAT's own domain vocabulary (searches surfaced only central-bank material, which is outside this cell). MONSTAT appears not to publish acceptance-infrastructure statistics at all.
negative_findings.result_summary: Acceptance-network counts are absent from the statistical-office estate.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's role is denominators only; the numerators (POS/ATM/card counts) must come from the central-bank cell, and any attempt to source them here will waste collection effort.

coverage_gaps.description: The Revenue and Customs Administration's own institutional pages (gov.me/upc) and its annual work reports were not directly fetched in this pass; the existence and contents of its publications section remain hypothesised from indirect evidence (a MONSTAT metadata entry referencing 'Pregled naplate prihoda Uprave carina').
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch gov.me/upc and its document library directly, in Montenegrin, and enumerate annual reports (godišnji izvještaj o radu) for fiscalization and revenue aggregates.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-SILC / income-and-living-conditions statistics for Montenegro (material deprivation, ability to meet unexpected expenses, bank-account-adjacent deprivation items) were not located in this pass, though MONSTAT lists social-protection and living-standard domains.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search 'Anketa o prihodima i uslovima života' / EU-SILC Crna Gora and add the release series as a financial-inclusion proxy denominator.

coverage_gaps.description: Adjacent national fiscal/oversight bodies were not covered: Državna revizorska institucija (State Audit Institution), Uprava za katastar i državnu imovinu, and the Central Register of Business Entities (CRPS) — the last being the authoritative merchant-population register that complements MONSTAT's statistical business register.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated local-language pass on 'Državna revizorska institucija', 'Centralni registar privrednih subjekata CRPS Crna Gora' and assess CRPS as the merchant denominator of record.

coverage_gaps.description: It is unknown whether MONSTAT grants researcher access to anonymised microdata (Household Budget Survey, ICT survey) and under what terms, and whether data.gov.me exposes a working CKAN API for Montenegrin publishers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Read MONSTAT's data-dissemination/confidentiality policy pages and probe data.gov.me's /api/3/action/package_list before committing to a collection architecture.

coverage_gaps.description: All Montenegrin-language searching used Latin script only. Montenegro also uses Cyrillic officially, and some institutional pages (e.g. data.gov.me /cnr/ locale) render in Cyrillic, so Cyrillic-form queries were not exercised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Repeat key queries in Cyrillic ('Управа за статистику', 'промет у трговини на мало', 'електронска фискализација') to test for additional or differently-indexed content.

brief: Montenegro's demand-side statistical landscape is dominated by one institution — MONSTAT (Uprava za statistiku) — which publishes, in mirrored Montenegrin/English HTML index pages backed by PDF and XLSX files, every denominator a payments analysis needs: annual Eurostat-aligned ICT household and enterprise surveys (with e-commerce and online-purchase indicators), monthly retail and wholesale turnover, monthly tourism arrivals and overnights, the multi-year Household Budget Survey, national accounts, CPI, the 2023 census and the statistical business register. Because ~96% of overnight stays are by foreign tourists, the tourism series is not a nice-to-have but the primary normaliser for a seasonal, non-resident-heavy card market. The fiscal side is thinner than the seed query assumed: the Ministry of Finance publishes budget-execution and public-debt reports rather than a named macroeconomic bulletin, while the highest-value asset in the cell — the Revenue and Customs Administration's mandatory e-fiscalization system, which records every cash and cashless invoice in real time since 2021 — publishes no payment-method statistics and would require a free-access-to-information request. Practical collection should key on MONSTAT's saopštenje/novosti archive index and release calendar rather than its unstable numeric page ids, with Eurostat's Montenegro (geo=ME) series and data.gov.me's CKAN catalogue as the machine-readable fallbacks.
